refnamediv.refpurpose: Primitive elements (generators of the multiplicative group) of a finite field

listitem.para: For n = 1: a row of integers in increasing order (the primitive roots modulo p).
For n > 1: a matrix with one element per row: α^k for every k in 1 .. p^n - 2 coprime to p^n - 1, in increasing order of k.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: An element is primitive when its powers give every non-zero element of the field, that is, when its multiplicative order is p^n - 1. A field of order q has φ(q - 1) primitive elements, φ being Euler's totient function.

For n > 1, α (a root of the primitive polynomial) is primitive, and α^k is primitive exactly when gcd(k, q - 1) = 1. For n = 1, the primitive elements are the powers r^k of the root r of the field's degree-1 polynomial, for the same values of k.
